scope_note: F12 is post-confirmatory descriptive/decision analysis. It does not create a new confirmatory hypothesis family and does not modify H1-H3.

internal_state_resource_analysis.reason_for_common_horizon_subset: The 20 contextual streams per scenario were prospectively extended to 5000 post-fork observations, so their state-arm resource totals are not commensurate with 2000-row primary forks. Resource comparisons therefore use only comparator_included=false streams, a pre-outcome hash-defined exclusion.
internal_state_resource_analysis.stream_summary: arithmetic mean of the two checkpoint-specific 2000-row fork metrics within each stream, then equal-scenario mean
internal_state_resource_analysis.primary_scientific_effect_source: F11 official all-4480-stream inference remains authoritative for H1/H2; the 4200-stream subset is used only for resource-commensurate paired economics.

material_resource_analysis.population: all eligible material checkpoints under the F09 H3 equal-scenario design-mixture ratio
material_resource_analysis.break_even: If retention has positive incremental APW and positive loss benefit, report APW premium per avoided prediction error and APW premium per one percentage point of loss reduction over the 2000-row horizon. If retention saves realised CPU/elapsed as well as loss, classify realised-compute dominance rather than inventing a break-even price.

contextual_comparator_analysis.outcome: full-stream prequential 0-1 mean loss over 24000 scored predictions
contextual_comparator_analysis.aggregation: equal-scenario arithmetic mean of per-stream cell metrics; all methods are paired on the same 280 source byte pairs

pareto.raw_2d: A method is dominated if another has no greater loss and no greater resource value with at least one strict improvement.
pareto.three_dimensional: loss + process CPU + mean peak RSS
pareto.supported_cpu_frontier: lower convex envelope in process-CPU versus loss; only methods that can minimise L + lambda*CPU for some lambda>=0 are called supported.

break_even.paired_loss_improvement: loss of cheaper method minus loss of more expensive method
break_even.cpu_premium: CPU seconds of more expensive method minus CPU seconds of cheaper method
break_even.scalarisation_lambda: paired_loss_improvement / cpu_premium in absolute loss per CPU second
break_even.unstable_rule: If the descriptive paired 95% bootstrap interval for loss improvement includes zero, the point break-even is reported as UNSTABLE_ACCURACY_INCREMENT and is not used for a recommendation.

uncertainty.role: descriptive sensitivity only; no new p-values or multiplicity family
uncertainty.resampling: whole stream within each scenario, preserving paired methods or checkpoint components
uncertainty.interval: 95% percentile interval using the 250th and 9750th one-based sorted bootstrap values
uncertainty.seed_rule: first 64 bits of SHA-256 over DT-C8E1-F12-v1|<analysis-name>|B=9999
uncertainty.ratio_rule: No redraw of undefined ratio replicates. Break-even ratios are not interval-estimated when their loss-improvement denominator is sign-unstable.

decision_rules.apw_firewall: APW is used only for internal F02/F05/F10 interventions and is never assigned to external comparators.
decision_rules.external_resource_firewall: CPU/elapsed/RSS/latency are realised implementation metrics and are never relabelled as APW or money.
decision_rules.money: No monetary conversion is permitted because no externally justified cost schedule was specified.
decision_rules.practical_equivalence_tie_break: When F11 classifies an internal loss contrast as EQUIVALENT, a lower-resource arm may be called operationally preferable under a lexicographic practical-equivalence rule, but not more accurate.
